name: RulZ Kinspora

approval.source: Owner, 2026-11-16 (releasing 0.9.0): "when it's ready, commit, create pr, merge and release. going forward always do this." Memory commit-and-push-after-every-update. Memory wiki-update-after-push (2026-11-11): "after every push or merge i would like you to update the wiki with changes." Destructive git (force push, history rewrite) still needs asking.

delivery.commitStyle: Plain sentence saying what the change does, phase in brackets when it is plan work, e.g. "Search the US National Archives with a key of the user's own (Phase 3e)".

changelog.entry: Date, link to the commit or PR, what changed.

wiki.rules: Home.md holds the status line; Roadmap.md the phase status, 'Waiting on outside parties' and decisions. New pages go in _Sidebar.md. Never use places or names from the owner's real Ancestry export as examples, in the wiki or anywhere else.

notes: Every release needs a "## <version>" section at the top of docs/RELEASE-NOTES.md, written in the PR: the release workflow takes the GitHub Release body from it and fails before the build without it. The workflow builds on the tag, uploads to a draft and publishes it, so installed copies offer the update from then on; check the release is published with the installer, its .blockmap and latest.yml. Stage changed files by name (never git add -A) and scan the diff for personal details before committing; say plainly in the report if a check failed. Watch the CI run on main after the push (ci.yml runs format, lint, typecheck, tests, e2e and the packaged-app test). pnpm format:check is left out of the local checks because Prettier flags the untracked AGENTS.md here; CI runs it. Run tools via package scripts: pnpm exec / pnpm vitest fail with "'node' is not recognized" on this PC. Run every wiki git command as git -C <wiki folder>. The project hook .claude/hooks/wiki-reminder.cjs reminds about the wiki after git push / gh pr merge and stays silent for pushes from a folder whose path contains 'wiki'. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md stay untracked: they were once pushed by mistake and erased from the public history.
